physics_goals.quote: The CRESST experiment aims at the direct detection of sub-GeV dark matter particles via elastic scattering off nuclei in different target crystals at cryogenic temperatures.
value: Direct detection of sub-GeV dark matter particles via elastic nuclear recoils in cryogenic crystal targets, with CRESST-III reaching thresholds of 10 eV and lower and probing WIMP masses down to ~70 MeV/c^2

summary.plain: CRESST looks for dark matter using crystals of calcium tungstate, cooled to a whisker above absolute zero deep under an Italian mountain. Each tiny bump from a passing particle makes both heat and a flash of light, and comparing the two tells physicists what kind of particle caused it.
summary.technical: Cryogenic scintillating-crystal calorimeter dark matter search at LNGS; proposed 1993, named CRESST in 1996. CRESST-I used sapphire absorbers (2000-2003); CRESST-II introduced 300 g CaWO4 crystals (2004-2015, Phase 2 to 2019); CRESST-III (from 2019) uses ~25 g crystals, reaching nuclear-recoil thresholds of 10 eV and lower and probing WIMP masses down to ~70 MeV/c^2, with detector R&D ongoing as of 2026.

unique_capabilities.quote: the simultaneous read-out of the deposited energy in the main absorber and an associated light signal
value: Simultaneous phonon (heat) and scintillation-light readout on cryogenic crystal absorbers for event-by-event background discrimination
